close_reason: Landed in commit b23e3e3. Option (c) ratified: doc-only hardening. Crate-level rustdoc 'Design: optional fields and Option<...>' section expanded with explicit partial-response exception explanation + table of the 8 mandatory-on-wire-but-Option fields. Each of the 5 Resource-derived structs (Calendar, CryptoKey, Directory, Link, Media) has a cross-reference paragraph. README Gotchas list gains a corresponding bullet. No type-shape change; the contract that callers MUST populate mandatory fields when building fresh values is now visible. Tests + clippy + rustdoc green on workspace.
description:
The crate documents in lib.rs:16-23 that mandatory RFC 9553 fields are modelled
as Option so partial-response inputs round-trip. The trade-off pushes the
'I cannot construct an invalid object' guarantee from the type system into
runtime checks the caller must write.

Concrete cases with mandatory-on-the-wire fields modelled as Option:

- Calendar.kind:515 ('Mandatory per RFC 9553 §2.4.1, modelled as Option')
- Calendar.uri:521 ('Mandatory on the wire per RFC 9553 §1.4.4')
- CryptoKey.uri:701 ('Mandatory per RFC 9553 §1.4.4')
- Directory.kind:744 ('Mandatory per RFC 9553 §2.6.2')
- Directory.uri:749 ('Mandatory per RFC 9553 §1.4.4')
- Link.uri:804 ('Mandatory per RFC 9553 §1.4.4')
- Media.kind:847 ('Mandatory per RFC 9553 §2.6.4')
- Media.uri:852 ('Mandatory per RFC 9553 §1.4.4')

A caller constructing Calendar { kind: None, uri: None, ... } and serializing
it produces a JSContact wire object no spec-conformant peer can validate. The
caller has no compile-time check, no Result-returning builder, no
into_wire_valid() method, no documented 'this method validates'.

The defensive code every consumer ends up writing:

  fn ensure_calendar_valid(c: &Calendar) -> Result<(), _> {
      if c.kind.is_none() || c.uri.is_none() { Err(...) } else { Ok(...) }
  }

…multiplied by the 8 mandatory-but-Option cases above and the 7 type-level
'at least one of X, Y, Z must be set' invariants documented on Name (line 88),
Organization (199), SpeakToAs (263), OnlineService (385), Address (584),
Author (1058).

Three resolutions, pick one:

(a) Add a #[doc(hidden)] (or pub-but-renamed) variant of each type with the
    mandatory fields bare (not Option), and a TryFrom<Wire> -> StrictForm
    conversion. Caller code working with their own data uses the strict form;
    only deserialize touches the lenient Option form.
(b) Add a fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), ConstructionError> method on each
    type with mandatory fields. Document that the caller MUST invoke validate
    before treating a fresh-constructed value as spec-conformant.
(c) Accept the trade-off but harden the documentation. The crate-level doc at
    lib.rs:16-23 acknowledges the choice; the per-field docs reiterate it. But
    there is no caller-facing helper or named contract. At minimum, add one
    section to the README's Gotchas list pointing this out.

Status quo (do nothing) is acceptable if and only if every downstream consumer
duplicates the validation. That bet has historically not paid off.
title: Mandatory RFC fields modelled as Option for partial-response permit constructing invalid wire objects
